title: A Password That Was Not a Secret
title_ja: 秘密ではなかったパスワード
fact_notes: 人物、場所、出来事、観察・実験の内容は架空の教材例。実在の研究結果や具体的なシステムの安全性を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A student team was developing a fictional online platform for sharing classroom announcements and wanted to make the registration process simple enough for new users.
sentences.ja: 生徒チームは教室の連絡事項を共有する架空のオンラインサービスを開発し、新規利用者に十分簡単な登録手続きにしたかった。

sentences.en: In the first prototype, a teacher could create a class and give every student the same short code to enter the shared classroom page.
sentences.ja: 最初の試作品では教師がクラスを作り共有ページに入る同じ短いコードを生徒全員に渡せた。

sentences.en: The developers had assumed that anyone who entered the correct code could be treated as an authorized member of that particular class.
sentences.ja: 開発者は正しいコードを入力する人は誰でもそのクラスの許可されたメンバーとして扱えると考えていた。

sentences.en: During a classroom demonstration, however, another student asked what would happen if the code were copied onto a publicly visible notice board.
sentences.ja: 教室での実演中、別の生徒はコードが公開掲示板に写されたら何が起こるか尋ねた。

sentences.en: The question encouraged the developers to distinguish the purpose of a classroom invitation from the purpose of verifying an individual's identity or permissions.
sentences.ja: その問いからクラスへの招待と個人の身元や権限の確認の目的を区別するようになった。

sentences.en: A shared code could help students identify which classroom they wanted to join, but it did not establish that every person who knew it had permission.
sentences.ja: 共有コードは参加したいクラスを特定する助けになっても、知っている全員に権限があるとは証明しなかった。

sentences.en: The team therefore reviewed which kinds of information would appear on the platform and which actions should be available only to particular users.
sentences.ja: そこでサービスにどのような情報が表示され、どの操作が特定の利用者だけに可能であるべきか見直した。

sentences.en: They recognized that the consequences of a mistaken decision about access would depend partly on what information and functions the system made available.
sentences.ja: アクセスの誤判断の結果はシステムが提供する情報や機能にも左右されると認識した。

sentences.en: Instead of attempting to make the shared classroom code impossible to copy, they redesigned the prototype so that a code would initiate a request to join.
sentences.ja: 共有コードをコピー不可能にしようとする代わりに、コードが参加申請のきっかけとなるよう試作を再設計した。

sentences.en: The teacher would then be able to review the request, and the system would distinguish ordinary classroom members from people responsible for managing the page.
sentences.ja: 教師が申請を確認でき、システムは一般のクラスメンバーと管理担当者を区別するようにした。

sentences.en: The developers also removed information from the demonstration that was unnecessary for the limited purpose of sharing announcements among the imaginary class members.
sentences.ja: 架空のクラスメンバー間で連絡を共有する限定目的に不要な情報を実演から削除した。

sentences.en: They prepared a separate checklist of questions about privacy and authorization that would need further attention before development of an actual service.
sentences.ja: 実際のサービス開発前にさらに注意が必要なプライバシーと認可についての質問を別の一覧にまとめた。

sentences.en: During a second demonstration, the students tested how the prototype responded when someone entered a valid invitation code without obtaining approval from the teacher.
sentences.ja: 第二の実演では教師の承認を得ず有効な招待コードを入力した場合の試作の応答を試した。

sentences.en: They also examined whether the responsibilities of ordinary users and administrators were clearly communicated through the instructions on the demonstration page.
sentences.ja: 通常利用者と管理者の責任が実演ページの指示で明確に伝わるかも調べた。

sentences.en: Although the revised design addressed the original misunderstanding, they did not claim that the platform had become secure enough for use with real student information.
sentences.ja: 改良設計は当初の誤解を解消したが実際の生徒情報を扱えるほど安全になったとは主張しなかった。

sentences.en: They explained that a more comprehensive security review would be necessary before a working platform could be introduced into an ordinary school environment.
sentences.ja: 実用サービスを通常の学校環境に導入する前により包括的な安全性確認が必要だと説明した。

sentences.en: The project illustrated how a convenient mechanism for identifying a shared activity can be mistaken for a mechanism for controlling access to private information.
sentences.ja: 活動は共有活動を特定する便利な仕組みが私的情報へのアクセスを管理する仕組みと混同され得ることを示した。

sentences.en: A useful design therefore needs to specify not only what a user can easily do but also what that user should be permitted to do.
sentences.ja: 有用な設計では利用者が簡単に何をできるかだけでなく何を許可されるべきか明確にする必要がある。

sentences.en: The students learned that reducing unnecessary data could be an important design decision, alongside measures intended to prevent unauthorized access.
sentences.ja: 不要な情報を減らすことも無許可アクセスを防ぐ対策と並ぶ重要な設計判断になり得ると学んだ。

sentences.en: For them, responsible software design began with clear questions about the purpose, limits, and ownership of the information being handled.
sentences.ja: 責任あるソフトウェア設計は扱う情報の目的、限界、所有について明確に問うことから始まった。

vocabulary.definition: the act of recording a new member
an early version made for testing

an act showing how something works
in a way accessible to the public
gave support or reason to act
the ability to enter or use something

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of the prototype?
options: Sell tickets to a public concert.
questions.explanation_ja: クラスの連絡事項の共有。

questions.prompt: What did the question about a public notice board expose?
options: Knowledge of a shared code might not prove authorization.
Students were unable to enter any code.
The board was too small to display information.
The developers had already verified every person's identity.
questions.explanation_ja: 共有コードだけで権限を確認できない。

questions.prompt: What distinction did the developers make?
options: An online platform differs from all forms of communication.
Inviting someone to a class differs from verifying permissions.
A teacher must never issue a classroom code.
Every code is automatically a private password.

questions.prompt: What affects the consequences of incorrect access decisions?
options: The color of the invitation code alone.
The number of letters in every announcement.
The size of the computer screen.
The information and functions made available.
questions.explanation_ja: アクセスできる情報・機能に左右される。

questions.prompt: What did the redesigned code initiate?

options: Information unnecessary for the demonstration's purpose.

questions.prompt: What was tested during the second demonstration?
options: The system's ability to predict final grades.
The safety of a fully deployed real service.
The response to a valid code without teacher approval.
questions.explanation_ja: 有効コードと承認のない場合を確認。

questions.prompt: Why did they avoid calling the platform secure?
options: They had found no possible improvements.
A fuller security review was still required before real use.
The platform had already been used by all schools.
Real student information was needed for every initial test.
questions.explanation_ja: 本番利用前に包括的な確認が必要。

questions.prompt: What does mechanism mean in context?
options: A system or method producing a result.
A personal opinion about a class.
A shared code alone is sufficient for all permissions.
Collecting more private data always improves security.
Convenient identification should be distinguished from authorized access and responsible data handling.
A successful demonstration proves a platform is safe for real use.
questions.explanation_ja: 識別と認可を区別し責任ある情報管理をする。

grammar.focus: what would happen if the code were copied
grammar.explanation_ja: 仮定法のif節が想定状況を示す。
butは利便性と権限確認の限界を対比する。

grammar.focus: so that a code would initiate a request to join
grammar.explanation_ja: so thatは目的・意図した結果。

grammar.focus: not only what a user can easily do but also what that user should be permitted to do
grammar.explanation_ja: not only A but also Bで両方を示す。

paraphrases.source: During a classroom demonstration, however, another student asked what would happen if the code were copied onto a publicly visible notice board.
paraphrases.rewrite: A student asked what could occur if someone displayed the shared code openly.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 公開された場合の影響を尋ねた。

paraphrases.source: A shared code could help students identify which classroom they wanted to join, but it did not establish that every person who knew it had permission.
paraphrases.rewrite: Knowing a code can identify a class without proving that the person is entitled to join it.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: コードはクラスを識別できても権限を証明しない。

paraphrases.source: Instead of attempting to make the shared classroom code impossible to copy, they redesigned the prototype so that a code would initiate a request to join.
paraphrases.rewrite: They changed the prototype so entering a code would begin a membership request rather than striving to prevent copying altogether.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: コードで申請が始まる設計に変更。

paraphrases.source: A useful design therefore needs to specify not only what a user can easily do but also what that user should be permitted to do.
paraphrases.rewrite: Good design must consider ease of use as well as the actions users are entitled to perform.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 利便性と許可される操作の両方を考える。

discourse.role_ja: 疑問から情報と権限を見直す。
コード自体を守る発想から申請手続きへ。
改善点と安全性確認の限界。

cloze.explanation_ja: 個人や権限を確認すること。
実際の情報を扱える安全性は未確認。
